newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan tightens security at Israel embassy.
newsitem.headline: Jordan tightens security at Israel embassy.

text.p: Jordan has recently tightened security around Israel's embassy in Amman in response to growing Arab-Israeli tension, an Israeli diplomat said on Monday.
He said Jordanian police were also trying to find out who had vandalised an unmarked hire car driven by a member of the embassy's administrative staff nearly two weeks ago.
"Jordan has decided to add security around the embassy. I think it is connected to the atmosphere, not the event with the car," embassy spokesman Shalom Tourgeman said.

Jordan's relations with Israel plunged in early March when King Hussein, seen as the Arab leader closest to Israel, rebuked Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for leading the Middle East into an "abyss of bloodshed."
Two days after his letter to Netanyahu was released a Jordanian soldier shot dead seven Israeli schoolgirls on Jordanian territory leased to Israel under a 1994 peace treaty.
Tourgeman said the embassy had complained to police after someone smashed a window and let the air out of the tyres of a car rented by embassy staff.
But he said diplomats at the embassy, inaugurated by Foreign Minister David Levy in December, were not taking any extra precautions.
"We lead a regular life. We don't act any differently. Life goes on," he said.
